Layout report for chublets.software (build 2026-10-09)
page: A0 portrait (841 x 1189 mm)
base text size chosen by autofit: 30.0 pt (range 28-30)
header title size: 90 pt
theme: chublets (chublets.software), state ready
  colours from: chublets house palette (CHUBLETS_PURPLE, CHUBLETS_GOLD) https://github.com/chublets-software/chublets-visuals (licence see the chublets-visuals repository)
  typeface: Fira Sans
  contrast: 26 pairings checked, 1 below the recommended level, lowest 4.38 (header event line)
body height: 974 mm available, 973 mm natural, slack 1 mm
note: autofit grew the body text to 30.0 pt because there was room. To keep it smaller and give figures the room instead, lower the cap (theme_overrides: typography: autofit: max_pt) or raise max_height_mm of the figures.

Blocks (why each one looks the way it does):
- hook: 358 mm wide, 93 mm natural, 93 mm drawn
    why: States the problem in two sentences: research software for heritage is scattered and thinly described.
- idea: 447 mm wide, 93 mm natural, 93 mm drawn
    why: Defines a chublet in one sentence and says what chublets.software is: the hub (author: it exists).
- journey: 813 mm wide, 106 mm natural, 106 mm drawn
    why: The backbone of the poster: six stations in order; all exist, the Federation Wikibase as a prototype.
- figures: 813 mm wide, 596 mm natural, 597 mm drawn
    why: One card for the six graphics from chublets-visuals: how it is modelled, the crosswalk behind it, the architecture.
- team: 180 mm wide, 154 mm natural, 154 mm drawn
    why: Puts names to faces once the photographs and consent are in (until then initials).
- links: 203 mm wide, 136 mm natural, 154 mm drawn
    why: Where the reader goes next: the demo and the Wikibase.
- supporters: 165 mm wide, 145 mm natural, 154 mm drawn
    why: Names funder, infrastructure and networks with their logos (usage terms to be checked, PRIMER D4).
- references: 240 mm wide, 153 mm natural, 154 mm drawn
    why: Lists the two repositories the poster describes and the sources of the data model.
